bib.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Hallucination Mitigation Techniques in Large Language Models

read.skipped: nothing; the paper has no appendices; reference list skimmed

question: How can the many techniques proposed to mitigate hallucination in LLMs be organised into one taxonomy, and what are their limits?
contributions: Introduction of a systematic taxonomy designed to categorize hallucination mitigation techniques for LLMs, encompassing Vision Language Models (VLMs).
Synthesis of the essential features characterizing these mitigation techniques, thereby guiding more structured future research endeavors within this domain.
Deliberation on the limitations and challenges inherent in these techniques, accompanied by potential solutions and proposed directions for future research.

results.claim: The survey covers more than thirty-two mitigation techniques.
results.setup: Survey of published work to Jan 2024; no experiments of its own
results.quote: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of over thirty-two techniques
results.note: The taxonomy figure and Table 1 list roughly 32 works.

results.claim: D&Q reaches 59.6% F1 on HotPotQA (question-only), as described by the survey.
results.setup: HotPotQA question-only setting; competitive with GPT-3.5 on ChitChatQA; as paraphrased by the survey
results.quote: achieving a noteworthy 59.6% F1 score on HotPotQA (question-only)
results.note: Only quantitative result in the survey.

results.claim: SynTra reduced hallucination for two 13B-parameter LLMs.
results.setup: Prefix-tuning of system message on a synthetic task, transferred to abstractive summarization
results.quote: Experiments demonstrate reduced hallucination for two 13B parameter LLMs
results.note: Model size, not an effect size.

results.claim: Taxonomy splits mitigation into Prompt Engineering (RAG before/during/after/end-to-end, self-refinement via feedback and reasoning, prompt tuning) and Developing Models (new decoding strategy, knowledge graph, faithfulness loss, supervised fine-tuning).
RAG is framed as mitigating hallucination by grounding in external authoritative knowledge, with retrieval timing (before, during, after generation) as the organising axis.
results.quote: RAG effectively mitigates the issue of hallucination in LLMs by generating responses that are not only pertinent and current but also verifiable

results.claim: Table 1 records per-method limitations, mostly extra compute or latency, narrow evaluation, single language or domain, or 'Details not provided'.
results.setup: Table 1, taken from each cited paper's own limitations
results.note: E.g. RARR 'computationally intensive'; CoVe 'only addresses hallucinations in the form of directly stated factual inaccuracies'; DoLa 'lacks external retrieval modules'. Several rows say 'Details not provided'.

limits: No experiments, no comparison of methods on a common benchmark; no numbers beyond one F1 and a model size, so nothing ranks techniques.
Every method description is the survey's paraphrase of another paper (often of its abstract); cite originals for results.
Authors concede only future directions (hybrid models, weak supervision, ethics); Section 5 lists no survey-specific limitations.
Coverage ends late 2023 and omits later RAG, self-correction and detection work; Table 1 column 'Detection' is a tick/cross with no definition of how detection was judged.
Duplicate Mündler 2023 reference; Mind's Mirror row in Table 1 repeats the EVER row's tasks, metrics, LLMs and datasets, so it looks copy-pasted and unreliable.
Taxonomy placement is loose: TWEAK (a decoding method) sits under supervised fine-tuning, and 'Developing Models' says it avoids fine-tuning then lists SFT.
practices: Ground generation in retrieved external knowledge, choosing retrieval before, during (sentence by sentence) or after generation (Sec 2.1.1).
Use feedback loops that verify a draft and revise it, as LLM-Augmenter, CoVe, Self-Reflection do (Sec 2.1.1.1, 2.1.2).
In CoVe, answer verification questions independently so the answers are unbiased (Sec 2.1.2).
Use contrastive decoding (CAD, DoLa) or activation shifts (ITI) when no retrieval or training is available (Sec 3.1).
Teach models to refuse questions outside their competence by appending refusal to uncertain training examples (R-Tuning, Sec 3.4).
Treat consecutive high-entropy words as one unit when masking and replacing (Sec 2.1.1.3).
Future: hybrid models combining mitigation approaches, weakly supervised learning, ethics review (Sec 5).

enhances the responses of LLMs by tapping into external, authoritative knowledge bases rather than relying on potentially outdated training data or the model's internal knowledge
the model's capacity to faithfully and properly reflect data from the input without adding errors, omissions, or distortions
adjusting the instructions provided to a pre-trained LLM during the fine-tuning phase; learns 'Soft Prompts' through backpropagation
LLM weights adjusted from gradients of a task-specific loss between predictions and ground truth labels
